name: TD SYNNEX CORPORATION
moat_justification: Real scale, breadth and Hyve's hyperscaler seat, but distribution is a thin-margin, low-switching-cost business where vendors and cloud marketplaces can route around the middleman and growth itself consumes working capital.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 4.8%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.1x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Real scale distributor, moat 4/10, but thin-margin AI volume is consuming cash (TTM OE negative on a working-capital build) and at $255.14 it does not clear 15% — it clears 15% only at or below $145.24.
moat_for: Largest-scale IT distributor — purchasing, logistics and credit capacity smaller rivals cannot match
Breadth: ~1,500 vendors, ~150,000 customers, 100+ countries; kept in Microsoft's consolidated distributor network
Hyve Solutions — direct hyperscaler design/build relationships peers do not hold the same way
Durable vendor/customer operating relationships across regions
moat_against: No pricing power — Q3 FY2026 gross margin contracted 61bp to 6.61% as AI volume surged
Low switching costs; head-on scale competition from Ingram Micro and Arrow; vendor-direct and cloud-marketplace disintermediation
Working-capital intensity — accelerating volume consumed cash in FY2026 (negative TTM OCF, $15.3B inventories)
Razor-thin earnings margin leaves little buffer against a hardware downcycle
